text.p: Malaysia's Advance Synergy Bhd (ASB) said on Friday it was seeking approval from the central bank to begin negotiations on merging its interest in financial services with another financial services firm.
It did not give other details in its statement to the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange but requested that the suspension of its stock be extended.
ASB stock was last traded on April 23 at 3.28 ringgit.
In a separate statement, ASB's financial services subsidiary, United Merchant Group Bhd said ASB plans to restructure the company.
United Merchant also requested for extension to the suspension of its stock. The company's shares were last traded on April 23 at 4.00 ringgit.
There has been market speculation that stockbroking and property firm Malpac Holdings Bhd was eyeing a stake in United Merchant.
Malpac on April 28 said it was seeking the approval from the central Bank Negara to start negotiations to acquire a stake in a financial firm.
